text:
kevin.s: heads-up — i'm trying to sketch the escape-hatch for canary traffic when the model variant starts returning partial_nacks and slow tails. starting a thread to align on interface shape.

olivia.k: high level goal? is this purely routing or do we need session/state migration?

kevin.s: both. we want fast fallback without losing user-visible context or duplicating heavy work. think: live requests have KV-cache, mid-stream generation state, and rerank context.

maria.t: nailed it. the messy bit is in-progress responses. if we abruptly switch routes, we either 1) drop the stream, 2) splice by resuming from KV cache on new variant, or 3) proxy remainder to fallback. each has tradeoffs.

dan_p: quick reality check: we can only resume if we have compatible tokenizer / kv layout. otherwise splice = impossible. we should detect compatibility at routing time.

kevin.s: proposal: policy DSL that describes fallback actions with a small capability handshake. e.g. capability: {kv_compatible: bool, seq_resume: bool, truncation_policy: [restart|continue|proxy]}.

olivia.k: can you paste a tiny example of that DSL?

kevin.s: sure — pseudo config: 
```
policy {
  condition: "latency > 500ms || errors.rate > 0.03"
  fallback: "variant-v2-lean"
  action: if kv_compatible && seq_resume then resume_else proxy
  proxy_ttl: 3s
  audit_tag: "canary-escape-2026"
}
```

maria.t: proxy_ttl is interesting — means the old route will accept a short-lived handoff where it finishes tokens and the new route picks up next requests?

kevin.s: yeah. sequence: 1) signal chosen fallback 2) old node will continue producing tokens for active streams for up to proxy_ttl 3) new route receives new requests (or resumed ones if capabilities allow) 4) router marks session affinity for follow-ups for N seconds.

dan_p: how do we decide affinity TTL? fixed vs adaptive? if too long we can pin traffic to a slow variant.

olivia.k: maybe adaptive — base on per-session tail latency and error history. also have a hard max (e.g., 60s) for pinned affinity.

maria.t: telemetry-wise we need fine-grained labels: origin_variant, fallback_variant, handoff_type (proxy|resume|restart), user_impacted boolean. otherwise alerts will be opaque.

kevin.s: agreed. also need a small RPC for capability negotiation: Router -> Candidate {model_name, model_hash} -> Candidate replies capabilities: [kv_layout_hash, token_schema, supports_resume:boolean]. use hashes to avoid leaking model internals.

dan_p: will require changes in the runtime agent. lightweight — compute a sha1 of kv layout and tokenizer config at startup and expose via health RPC.

olivia.k: what about cold requests mid-handoff? e.g., request arrives to router while old node is finishing proxied stream. router must prefer new variant for new requests if policy says fallback, but ensure ongoing streams aren't interrupted.

maria.t: that's standard: priority rules: 1) keep existing streams on their node until proxy_ttl expires 2) new requests go to fallback 3) if resume supported, try to reconstruct with resume path.

kevin.s: there's also cost accounting: if we allow old node to finish long-running streams while routing new ones to cheap fallback, costs bifurcate. need per-session billing tags.

dan_p: ops question — how do we roll back the fallback decision quickly if the fallback performs worse? we need a fast reverse signal and hysteresis to prevent flip-flopping.

olivia.k: add a kill-switch at router level + require fallback acceptance only after stability window (like 30s) and allow immediate undo via operator API. also add rate-limit for automations: no more than 1 auto-fallback per 5m for same service.

maria.t: corner case: multi-tenant host where a single GPU serves mixed tenants. fallback by variant could lead to noisy neighbor effects. policy should support tenant-scoped overrides.

kevin.s: yes — policy scoping: global, tenant, route. router should evaluate in order: tenant policy -> route policy -> global.

dan_p: we should avoid huge statefulness in router. Keep router mostly policy-evaluator + short-lived session map. Persist affinity entries to in-memory store with TTL, not durable.

olivia.k: for audit and for postmortems, emit an event when fallback triggers with snapshot: {policy, metrics_snapshot, selected_action}. that can feed Optimize for model/regression alerts.

maria.t: question: do we need a standardized error taxonomy from runtime so router can reason (partial_nack vs token_drop vs slow_tail)?

kevin.s: yes — minimal taxonomy: OK, SOFT_FAIL (recoverable partial), HARD_FAIL (cannot continue), SLOW_TAIL (latency degradation), COMPAT_MISMATCH. router acts differently per class.

dan_p: implement plan sketch for runtime changes: 1) capability RPC 2) emit error taxonomy events 3) accept handoff/proxy handshake API 4) opt-in resume support behind an experimental flag.

olivia.k: timeline? can we prototype in 2 weeks with router-side simulation and runtime feature flags?

maria.t: two weeks for a prototype simulation sounds right. production rollout requires thorough canary of the escape-hatch itself.

kevin.s: next steps: olivia will draft policy DSL + decision table. dan will add capability RPC stub in runtime. maria will draft telemetry/event schema. i'll wire a router simulation to test handoff flows.

olivia.k: acked. i'll post a short RFC draft by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: auto-note: created task CANARY-ESCAPE-HATCH-2026 assigned to olivia.k, dan_p, maria.t, kevin.s. due 2026-04-08."
